title: Staged patch escrow and safety rollback procedure for LTS & GA rollouts
creator: Riley Thompson
description: Establish a reusable, auditable process for staging emergency patches (patch escrow), coordinated backports to supported LTS channels, and automated safety rollback gates for GA rollouts. This ticket captures decision criteria for severity -> patch cadence, naming conventions for escrow branches and hotfix tags, rollback automation runbooks, test requirements for a safe rollback, and integration points with the Console/observability dashboards. The goal is to reduce mean time to safe rollback and ensure backports are reproducible across dedicated/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Patch escrow workflow documented and reviewed by Eng + Security + Product
CLI automation to create escrow branch + signed patch tag (redwood-escrow/<release>-<patch>) exists and is tested in a dry-run
Rollback gate (automated health checks + manual abort conditions) is wired into the canary rollout pipeline for runtime-1.22
Backport matrix and branch naming convention published; at least one backport PR created for LTS-1 and verified through CI
Runbook for oncall (2-step rollback: canary abort then full rollback) published and linked from PagerDuty incident page
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose 'patch escrow' model over immediate hotfix branching to allow triage window for telemetry. Rationale: telemetry often surfaces cross-service regressions; escrow window (1-4 hours depending on severity) reduces risk of rushed incomplete fixes. (Marisol)
2026-03-04: Agreed severity thresholds: S0 (sev0) -> immediate patch + <10m mitigation channel; S1 -> escrow 1hr; S2 -> escrow 4-24hr. Decision recorded after simulated drills. (Riley, Priya Gupta)
2026-03-08: Decided to require signed patch tags for any release touching customer data paths (KMS/encryption) and to open a security review checklist item. (Security)
rollout_steps: Create escrow branch: redwood-escrow/<major>.<minor>.<patch>-<ticket> (CLI helper will populate changelog stub)
Open patch PR against escrow branch; run full regression CI and smoke on canary infra; attach smoke URLs and Grafana panel captures
Promote patch to canary with staged percentages: 1% -> 5% -> 20% (minimum 30 minutes per stage) with automated SLO checks at each stage
If canary SLO breach or error spike: pipeline triggers 'canary abort' and executes rollback playbook (step 1: remove traffic to canary; step 2: if expanded beyond canary, initiate full rollback)
Post-rollback root cause triage: create follow-up ticket with RCA, link to the escrow branch and artifact bundle
patch_branch_policy: Escrow branches live for 48 hours by default. Hotfixes created from escrow must be cherry-picked into LTS-1 and LTS-2 maintained branches within 72 hours. Branch naming: redwood-escrow/<release>-<ticket>, hotfix branches: hotfix/<release>-<ticket>-<short-desc>. Tags: signed tag format 'escrow-<release>-<ticket>-v<patch>'. All patches must include 'rollback-ready' flag in PR template (checkboxes for migration safety, config toggles, and feature flags).
backport_matrix: Targets: GA latest (non-LTS), LTS (active) and LTS-previous (maintenance). Backport priority: LTS-active first, then LTS-previous if regression affects customer-facing APIs. Backport rules: avoid code that requires large refactors. If backport requires >2 files modified, escalate to SE for approval. Required artifacts: repro test case, small scoped patch, changelog entry. Backport testing: run smoke + minimal e2e subset on private deployment image.
test_plan: Add rollback unit/integration tests exercising kv-cache warm/cold state transitions
Automated canary SLO checks: latency P99, error rate, request success ratio; thresholds stored in console-params
Dry-run automation that simulates canary abort without changing traffic (CI step)
automation_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts/pulls/219 (CLI escrow helper and dry-run unit tests)
notes: We ran two simulated drills (2026-03-05, 2026-03-09) using a synthetic latency regression; average mitigation time reduced by 32% when using escrow flow vs immediate branching.

Follow-up work: integrate console-visible 'rollback readiness' indicator (separate ticket), and add RBAC gate for private deployments where Legal review is required before rollback on customer-owned infra.
